meta.description: Benign SQL syntax-boundary probes for error-based SQL Injection detection. These markers are designed to break SQL query structure and elicit DBMS error messages WITHOUT executing any destructive SQL statements.
meta.usage: Append each boundary string to a parameter value. Match the HTTP response body against the DBMS error patterns defined below.

boundary_probes.description: Classic single-quote string terminator — most common SQLi trigger
Double-quote string terminator — used in MySQL ANSI mode and MSSQL
Closes a string AND a parenthesised expression — targets function call contexts
Double-quote variant of the parenthesis-close probe
SQL line comment — neutralises the remainder of the original query
Tautology probe — always-true condition to detect Boolean-based blind SQLi via response size diff
Contradiction probe — always-false condition pair for Boolean blind detection
MySQL identifier quote character — can cause syntax errors in MySQL
Statement separator — reveals stacked-query support (PostgreSQL, MSSQL)

time_based_probes.description: Boolean-context SLEEP() — reliable blind-injection timing oracle for MySQL/MariaDB.
Stacked-query pg_sleep() — requires the driver to allow multiple statements.
Stacked-query WAITFOR DELAY — native MSSQL timing primitive.

time_based_probes.value: ' AND 1=(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ALL_USERS T1,ALL_USERS T2,ALL_USERS T3,ALL_USERS T4,ALL_USERS T5)-- -
time_based_probes.description: Cartesian-product heavy query — Oracle has no unprivileged native sleep, so delay is induced via computation cost instead.

dbms_error_patterns.description: Compiled regex patterns matching known DBMS error strings. Keys are DBMS names; values are lists of regex patterns. All patterns are case-INSENSITIVE.

MySQL: you have an error in your sql syntax
supplied argument is not a valid mysql result
column count doesn't match value count
MariaDB: mariadb server version for the right syntax
PostgreSQL: unterminated quoted string at or near
supplied argument is not a valid postgresql result
MSSQL: unclosed quotation mark after the character string
microsoft ole db provider for sql server
Generic: unexpected end of command in statement

false_positive_filter.description: Strings that, if present in the BASELINE (unmodified) response, indicate the server ALREADY returns database errors. Matches here should cause the finding to be suppressed as a pre-existing condition.
